result.title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
result.comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery: Bridging the Translation Gap (AI4DD). Code and data: https://github.com/jackysiupuichung/forecast-or-know
result.summary: AI systems increasingly help decide which drug targets enter costly clinical trials. We recast each target-disease hypothesis as a dated event, the pair's first clinical trial. This lets us test whether a language model can forecast such events after its training cutoff, rather than recall events before it. We rebuild a dated biomedical knowledge graph as it stood at the end of each year from 2020 up to its newest version. We then ask six open language models, with and without this graph, which targets will enter a first trial for a disease the next year. Without retrieval, the models rank about as well as trial history, a count of each target's past trials in the same therapeutic area, also after their training cutoffs. Evidence dated before the decision adds at most a small gain, before or after the models' training cutoffs. The newest graph raises five of six models clearly above that baseline, but its paths usually include the answer: the pair's own trial, dated after the decision. Evaluations of target prioritisation should date both features and labels, with evidence from before the decision and outcomes after it.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把「靶点—疾病」假设重构为带日期的事件（首次临床试验），重建截至各年末的生物医学知识图谱，检验六个开源语言模型能否在训练截止之后预测新事件而非回忆旧事件，并指出最新图谱带来的提升多来自路径中已含未来答案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据须早于决策、标签须晚于决策」的时间泄漏审计，以及区分「预测」与「已知」的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否已隐含答案、视觉证据是否真被使用等因果与贡献分配评价设计。
